problem: Eviction now resets at fixed multiples of window instead of sliding (now - window, now], so up to 2x limit requests are accepted across a bucket boundary.
retry_after still uses q[0] + window - now, which contradicts the new bucket eviction and returns values that are too short or too long.
Bucket floor arithmetic depends on absolute clock alignment (e.g. -1 and 0 fall in different buckets) and is subject to float rounding with float windows.
setdefault creates a deque for every key, including on read-only calls, and empty deques are never removed, so caller-supplied keys grow memory without bound.
The semantic change to window eviction ships with no tests, and none pin boundary behaviour or retry_after.
Inline __import__("collections").deque() duplicates the existing deque import and setdefault allocates a throwaway deque on every call.
The comment documenting the window boundary semantics was deleted and not replaced.
